Here are the search results covering Obsidian vault MCP servers with markdown frontmatter support and pytest-based testing strategies:

---

## Key Projects Found

### 1. **markdown-frontmatter-mcp** (by caffeinatedwes)
A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that queries Markdown files by front matter metadata, designed for Obsidian vaults and other Markdown-based knowledge bases. Existing tools can search by keywords or do semantic search, but none let you query by front matter metadata — filtering by tags AND recency. It exposes a `query_recent_notes` tool that filters by tags, how far back to look (days), which folders to search, and max results. For testing, you can set your KB path and run the server directly for testing with `python3 src/server.py`.

### 2. **mcp-obsidian** (by bitbonsai)
A universal AI bridge for Obsidian vaults using the Model Context Protocol (MCP) standard, connecting any MCP-compatible AI assistant to your knowledge base. This server provides safe read/write access to your notes while preventing YAML frontmatter corruption. Security features include YAML Frontmatter Validation (parsed and validated before writing), Function/Symbol Prevention (dangerous JavaScript objects blocked from frontmatter), and Data Type Checking (only safe data types allowed).

### 3. **obsidian-mcp** (by punkpeye) — with pytest testing
Features include tag management (supporting both frontmatter and inline tags), link management, note insights, and AI-optimized error messages. This project has a comprehensive **pytest-based testing strategy**:
You can run all tests with `python tests/run_tests.py`, run specific test types including unit tests (requires pytest), integration tests (requires pytest), and live tests with real Obsidian, or run individual test files like `test_comprehensive.py` for full workflow tests and `test_data_validation.py` for data structure validation.

### 4. **obsidian-mcp-server** (by Vasallo94) — with pytest testing
This project also uses pytest extensively. Tests can be run with `uv run pytest`, with verbose output via `uv run pytest -v`, or for a specific test class like `uv run pytest tests/test_basic.py::TestConfiguration`. The test suite uses anyio for asynchronous tests. The project has a modular structure with tools organized by category (navigation, creation, analysis), resources, prompts, shared utilities, and includes `pytest.ini` for test configuration.

### 5. **markdown-editor-mcp-server** (by KazKozDev)
This is an MCP server providing tools for structured, semantic editing of Markdown files that understands the logical structure of documents, and is fully compliant with MCP 2025 Standard. Many Markdown tools (Obsidian, Jekyll) use YAML metadata at the top, and this tool allows the LLM to manage tags, dates, and properties without messing with the body text by updating or adding YAML Frontmatter to the document. Testing is straightforward: install for development with `pip install -e .` and run tests with `pytest tests/`.

### 6. **obsidian-mcp-server** (by cyanheads)
An Obsidian Knowledge-Management MCP server that enables AI agents and development tools to interact with an Obsidian vault, providing a comprehensive suite of tools for reading, writing, searching, and managing notes, tags, and frontmatter, acting as a bridge to the Obsidian Local REST API plugin. It atomically manages a note's YAML frontmatter with get, set, or delete operations on frontmatter keys. It features an intelligent in-memory vault cache service that improves performance, provides a fallback if the live API fails, and periodically refreshes to stay in sync.

---

## Summary of Testing Strategies

| Project | Testing Approach |
|---|---|
| **punkpeye/obsidian-mcp** | Unit, integration, and live tests via pytest; separate test files for workflows and data validation |
| **Vasallo94/obsidian-mcp-server** | pytest with anyio for async tests; `pytest.ini` config; specific test classes |
| **markdown-editor-mcp-server** | Simple `pytest tests/` execution |
| **markdown-frontmatter-mcp** | Manual server testing via direct execution |

The most mature pytest-based testing strategies are found in the **punkpeye/obsidian-mcp** and **Vasallo94/obsidian-mcp-server** projects, which separate tests into unit, integration, and live tiers.

Here's a comprehensive overview of **MCP Server Incremental Adoption Strategy, Existing Tools Migration, and Best Practices (2025)**:

---

## Overview of MCP Adoption in 2025

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard, open-source framework introduced by Anthropic in November 2024 to standardize how AI systems—particularly LLMs—integrate with and access external tools, systems, and data sources. Think of MCP as "USB-C for AI applications"—a universal connector that allows any AI model to communicate with any tool through a single, standardized interface.

Organizations are reporting 30% reductions in development overhead and 50-75% time savings on common tasks. Major AI providers including OpenAI, Anthropic, Hugging Face, and LangChain began standardizing around MCP in 2025, establishing MCP as the core integration interface across AI-native ecosystems.

---

## Incremental Adoption Strategy

### Adapter-First / Phased Approach

The key principle is **incremental adoption**: avoid big-bang migrations. Build confidence with small, controlled phases.

The recommended approach is to **adopt incrementally**: for each integration point, develop an MCP server that wraps the application's API or control surface (REST, SDK, scripting, etc.), and roll out MCP adapters in phases, starting with the lowest-risk, highest-reward integrations.

During migration, **run both custom and MCP integrations side-by-side** (parallel running) to ensure no loss of functionality.

**Establish rollback mechanisms**: prepare to revert quickly if any MCP adapter introduces instability.

Then **expand coverage**: gradually migrate remaining custom integrations to MCP as the ecosystem matures.

### Assessment Before Adoption

A practical framework helps you figure out whether MCP servers are right for your specific use case by systematically checking eight critical constraint categories. Each constraint gets scored, and the combined assessment guides your decision.

Key principles: context matters more than technology; start small and prove value—even strong candidates benefit from pilot projects; and reassess regularly as the ecosystem matures.

---

## Migrating Existing Tools

For organizations accustomed to custom integrations, the migration to MCP can be transformative, simultaneously reducing technical debt and unlocking new interoperability benefits. The playbook provides a structured, repeatable approach with an emphasis on adapters—lightweight servers that bridge your existing software stack to the protocol's standardized interface.

For **legacy systems**, consider building compatibility shims that expose legacy interfaces via MCP adapters.

Companies often start off deploying a local/workstation MCP server (because they're easier to build), only later updating it to a remote server.

Early adopters reported several obstacles during deployment: technical complexity when mapping MCP tools to internal systems, and change management friction across IT, security, and business users.

---

## Best Practices for MCP Servers

### Tool Design
**Define a clear toolset**: avoid mapping every API endpoint to a new MCP tool. Instead, group related tasks and design higher-level functions. Overloading the toolset increases server complexity, deployment cost, and can deter users. Focused tool selection was found to improve user adoption by up to 30%.

### Security
**OAuth 2.1 is now mandatory** for HTTP-based transports as of the March 2025 specification update. Don't use session IDs for auth, generate non-predictable session identifiers, verify all authorized requests, and minimize data exposure.

**Security by design**: limit network exposure of MCP adapters. Use authentication, encryption, and access controls as appropriate for your environment.

### Idempotency & Transport
Your server will be called by agents that may retry or parallelize requests. Make tool calls idempotent, accept client-generated request IDs, and return deterministic results for the same inputs. Use pagination tokens and cursors for list operations.

Support **stdio** for maximum client compatibility today, and add **Streamable HTTP** when you need networked, horizontally scalable servers. The SSE transport has been deprecated and replaced by Streamable HTTP in the 2025-06-18 specification.

### Documentation & Versioning
Provide clear API references, environment requirements, tool descriptions, and sample requests. Well-documented MCP servers see **2x higher developer adoption rates** compared to undocumented ones.

Use **semantic versioning**: tag MCP server releases and tools semantically and maintain a changelog. This streamlines client upgrades and rollbacks.

### Team Enablement
**Train teams**: upskill developers, data scientists, and operations staff on MCP concepts, SDK usage, and adapter development.

**Update documentation** and maintain clear, searchable records of all MCP adapters. Cultivate a community by encouraging internal sharing of adapter templates, best practices, and troubleshooting tips.

### Testing
Ensure adapters properly advertise their capabilities through MCP's tool discovery mechanism. Subject each adapter to robust integration and regression testing, including edge cases and failure modes.

---

## Enterprise Outlook

Despite the momentum, many enterprises are taking a measured approach. IT leaders in regulated or large organizations see the promise of MCP's standardization but want to see the ecosystem mature further before full commitment.

2026 marks the transition from experimentation to enterprise-wide adoption. The December 2025 donation of MCP to the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) under the Linux Foundation ensures MCP remains vendor-neutral while benefiting from decades of experience stewarding critical open-source infrastructure.

**Implementation Highlights:**

- **4-Phase Incremental Roadmap** — Foundation (Resources + schema) → Bridge (BMAD sync tools) → Intelligence (Prompts + Canvas) → Enhancement (FTS5 + validation). Total: 6-10 days
- **8 New MCP Tools** — `bmad_sync_artifact`, `bmad_list_artifacts`, `bmad_generate_canvas`, etc. for full BMAD-vault integration

Here's a comprehensive overview of the **Obsidian + MCP knowledge management AI workflow** landscape and future outlook for 2026:

---

## Obsidian's Growth & Position in 2026

As of February 2026, Obsidian crossed 1.5 million users with 22% year-over-year growth. The reason is clear: in an era where AI is reshaping how we work, Obsidian's local-first, Markdown-based approach makes it the ideal foundation for an AI-powered second brain.

As of 2026, Obsidian has introduced game-changing new features, most notably native AI integration for note synthesis, real-time collaboration for shared vaults, and a significantly overhauled mobile experience. These updates solidify its position as the leading personal knowledge management (PKM) tool for those who value privacy and power.

---

## MCP Integration: The Big Development

The most exciting development in 2026 is connecting Claude Code (Anthropic's CLI agent) to Obsidian via MCP (Model Context Protocol). This turns your vault into a live workspace that Claude can read, search, and modify.

The Obsidian MCP Server is a knowledge-management MCP server that enables AI agents and development tools to interact with an Obsidian vault, providing a comprehensive suite of tools for reading, writing, searching, and managing notes, tags, and frontmatter.

MCP Tools enables AI applications like Claude Desktop to securely access your vault through the Model Context Protocol — the new industry standard that OpenAI and Anthropic adopted in 2025.

### What MCP Enables

By integrating Claude with Obsidian using MCP, Claude can read, organise, and restructure your Obsidian vault, generate summaries, build dashboards, and surface insights, all without leaving your workspace.

The MCP server allows applications like AI assistants, IDE extensions, or custom scripts to interact directly with your Obsidian vault — automating vault management, integrating Obsidian into AI workflows for research/writing/coding tasks, and building custom tools that interact with vault data in novel ways.

---

## AI-Powered Workflows in Practice

The concept is simple but powerful: your notes become a knowledge base that AI can read, search, and reason over. Instead of starting every AI conversation from scratch, you give it access to everything you've ever written — research, meeting notes, project plans, code snippets, personal reflections.

What started as a one-time analysis has become an ongoing partnership, with regular use of MCP-connected Claude for content development support, quality maintenance, and research and writing assistance.

With this setup, because the entire knowledge base is stored locally in Obsidian and accessed via MCP configuration files, switching AI accounts is trivial — the "brain" persists locally, independent of the specific LLM account instance.

---

## Key Plugins & Ecosystem

Smart Connections (600,000+ downloads) creates semantic maps across your entire knowledge base using AI embeddings, with everything staying local. For someone with 5+ years of notes, it becomes genuinely powerful, identifying missing connections based on meaning.

Obsidian's local-first architecture means you're not locked into any single AI provider — you can use Claude, GPT, Gemini, or fully local models.

---

## Future Outlook

We're at an inflection point in how humans manage knowledge. The combination of local AI, visual thinking tools, database functionality, and external AI integration via MCP creates possibilities that didn't exist even six months ago.

AI integrations should let us leverage our notes at scale, and AI should easily connect to our knowledge bases to find, use, and update information. This is possible today through MCP, but there's a "gazillion more things" AI already enables for knowledge management yet to be discovered.

Speech-to-text and text-to-speech should become much more important in the future of knowledge management. Tools for Thought should be fully controllable through voice and fully integrated with AI, making it possible to easily create and add new notes with AI connecting the dots.

For anyone serious about knowledge management, research, or learning, MCP-enabled AI analysis isn't just a productivity tool — it's a new way of thinking about how human intelligence and artificial intelligence can work together.

---

In summary, the Obsidian + MCP + AI ecosystem in 2026 represents a maturing paradigm where personal knowledge bases become active, AI-queryable workspaces rather than passive note storage, with the future pointing toward deeper voice integration, more seamless AI collaboration, and increasingly automated knowledge graph maintenance.

Technology Landscape Summary\n\n**Obsidian Core:** Local-first markdown with 7 typed properties (text, list, number, checkbox, date, datetime, tags), vault-wide type enforcement, Canvas (open JSON spec), Dataview query engine, Templater automation (3.8M+ downloads).\n\n**MCP Ecosystem:** 3 primitives (Tools, Resources, Prompts), Streamable HTTP transport (replaces deprecated SSE), capability-based negotiation, MCP Registry (~2,000 servers), donated to AAIF under Linux Foundation (Dec 2025).\n\n**Our Server:** 47 tools, 12 categories, ~10,475 lines Python, FastMCP on port 8360.      1→# Project Context: Cohezion Compound Engineering
     2→
     3→_Purpose: LLM-optimized reference for compound engineering implementation. Read before coding._
     4→
     5→---
     6→
     7→## Core Identity
     8→
     9→- **Project**: Cohezion — The Observatory for Artificial Cosmogenesis
    10→- **Methodology**: FLUME (Dual-state manifold reasoning with VAE latent space)
    11→- **Hardware**: AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 (128GB LPDDR5X unified memory)
    12→
    13→---
    14→
    15→## Compound Engineering Patterns
    16→
    17→### Session Lifecycle (Warm-Start / Clean-Shutdown)
    18→
    19→```python
    20→from cohezion.compound.session_manager import CompoundSessionManager
    21→
    22→async with CompoundSessionManager() as mgr:
    23→    summary = mgr.start_session(max_cache_entries=256)
    24→    # ... compound cycles ...
    25→    result = mgr.end_session()
    26→```
    27→
    28→**Rules:**
    29→- Always use context manager for clean shutdown
    30→- `start_session()` loads warm cache and metrics snapshot
    31→- `end_session()` persists cache and saves metrics snapshot
    32→
    33→### Checkpoint Persistence
    34→
    35→| Storage | Primary | Fallback |
    36→|---------|---------|----------|
    37→| Checkpoints | Vault MCP (`mcp.vault_write`) | Local JSONL in `data/checkpoints/` |
    38→| Cache | Vault MCP | Local JSONL in `data/cache/` |
    39→
    40→**Pattern:**
    41→```python
    42→from cohezion.compound.cache_persistence import CachePersistence, WarmCacheLoader
    43→
    44→# On start: warm cache
    45→loader = WarmCacheLoader()
    46→entries_loaded = loader.warm_client(client, max_entries=256)
    47→
    48→# On end: persist cache
    49→cp = CachePersistence()
    50→cp.save_cache(client._cache)
    51→```
    52→
    53→### FLUME VAE (256D Latent Space)
    54→
    55→- **Location**: `src/cohezion/flume/`
    56→- **Architecture**: Encoder → 256D latent → Decoder
    57→- **Purpose**: Transform raw requests into manifold coordinates
    58→- **Integration**: Called in `CompoundExecutor` Step 3 (Manifest)
    59→
    60→### 12D Universe Journey Tracking
    61→
    62→```python
    63→from cohezion.compound.journey_tracker import JourneyTracker
    64→
    65→tracker = JourneyTracker()
    66→state = tracker.record_state(
    67→    agent_id="agent-1",
    68→    phase="execution",
    69→    position={"x": 0.5, "y": 0.3, "z": 0.7},  # 3D base
    70→    coherence=0.85,
    71→    # 9 additional dimensions auto-expanded
    72→)
    73→```
    74→
    75→**Dimensions**: x, y, z (spatial) + coherence + energy + entropy + momentum + phase + velocity + amplitude + frequency
    76→
    77→### Request Alignment Coherence Scoring
    78→
    79→```python
    80→from cohezion.compound.request_alignment_analyzer import RequestAlignmentAnalyzer
    81→
    82→analyzer = RequestAlignmentAnalyzer()
    83→alignment = analyzer.analyze(request, available_skills, agent_context)
    84→if alignment.coherence < 0.5:
    85→    logger.warning(f"Low alignment: {alignment.issues}")
    86→```
    87→
    88→**Threshold**: Coherence < 0.5 requires human review
    89→
    90→### Cost-Aware Model Routing
    91→
    92→```python
    93→from cohezion.swarm.cost_aware_router import CostAwareRouter
    94→
    95→router = CostAwareRouter()
    96→model = router.select_model(task_complexity=0.7, budget_remaining=0.50)
    97→```
    98→
    99→**Model Tiers**:
   100→| Tier | Use Case | Cost |
   101→|------|----------|------|
   102→| Local (Ollama) | Simple extraction, classification | $0 |
   103→| Cloud (Claude) | Complex reasoning, multi-step | $3-15/M tokens |
   104→
   105→---
   106→
   107→## Critical Implementation Rules
   108→
   109→### Async / I/O
   110→
   111→- **ALL** I/O must be `async/await` with timeouts
   112→- Never use blocking calls in async contexts
   113→- Global Ollama limit: 4 concurrent requests
   114→
   115→### Testing
   116→
   117→- **Mock at source**: `@patch("cohezion.module.function")` — NOT at consumer
   118→- **Singleton reset**: Reset in `tests/conftest.py` between tests
   119→- **Fixtures**: Use `mock_ollama`, `mock_surreal` for unit tests
   120→- **Markers**: `@pytest.mark.fast` (<1s, no live services)
   121→
   122→### Type Safety
   123→
   124→- Mandatory type hints on all public signatures
   125→- Use modern syntax: `list[int]`, `str | None`
   126→- mypy `--strict` compatible
   127→
   128→### Import Management
   129→
   130→- Standard library → Third-party → Local (`cohezion`)
   131→- Never use `ruff --unsafe-fixes` (breaks mock.patch targets)
   132→
   133→---
   134→
   135→## Project Structure
   136→
   137→```
   138→src/cohezion/
   139→├── compound/       # 11-step executor, skill refiner, retrospection
   140→├── swarm/          # Team orchestration, cost routing
   141→├── cache/          # L1/L2/L3 semantic cache
   142→├── flume/          # VAE encoder (256D latent)
   143→├── skills/         # PRIME skill definitions (*.md)
   144→├── api/            # FastAPI backend (72 endpoints)
   145→└── core/           # Persistence, repositories
   146→```
   147→
   148→---
   149→
   150→## Key Classes
   151→
   152→| Class | File | Purpose |
   153→|-------|------|---------|
   154→| `CompoundExecutor` | `compound/executor.py` | 11-step pipeline orchestrator |
   155→| `CompoundSessionManager` | `compound/session_manager.py` | Lifecycle management |
   156→| `JourneyTracker` | `compound/journey_tracker.py` | 12D state recording |
   157→| `RequestAlignmentAnalyzer` | `compound/request_alignment_analyzer.py` | Coherence scoring |
   158→| `CostAwareRouter` | `swarm/cost_aware_router.py` | Model selection |
   159→| `GlobalMetricsAggregator` | `compound/global_metrics_aggregator.py` | Metrics collection |
   160→
   161→---
   162→
   163→## Build Commands
   164→
   165→```bash
   166→make format        # ruff format
   167→make lint          # ruff check --fix
   168→make type-check    # mypy
   169→make test-fast     # pytest -m fast
   170→make test          # Full suite (~90s)
   171→```
   172→
   173→---
   174→
   175→## Anti-Patterns (Never Do)
   176→
   177→- Block I/O in async handlers
   178→- Mock after import (`@patch("cohezion.api.client")`)
   179→- Use bare `pip` instead of `uv`
   180→- Skip type hints "for speed"
   181→- Hardcode credentials (use Vault)
   182→
   183→---
   184→
   185→## References
   186→
   187→- `_bmad-output/project-context.md` — Full project context
   188→- `tests/conftest.py` — Singleton reset fixtures
   189→- `.agent/CONSTITUTION.md` — Behavioral constraints
   190→- `AGENTS.md` — Coding standards
   191→

     1→# Project Context: Cohezion Compound Engineering
     2→
     3→_Purpose: LLM-optimized reference for compound engineering implementation. Read before coding._
     4→
     5→---
     6→
     7→## Core Identity
     8→
     9→- **Project**: Cohezion — The Observatory for Artificial Cosmogenesis
    10→- **Methodology**: FLUME (Dual-state manifold reasoning with VAE latent space)
    11→- **Hardware**: AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 (128GB LPDDR5X unified memory)
    12→
    13→---
    14→
    15→## Compound Engineering Patterns
    16→
    17→### Session Lifecycle (Warm-Start / Clean-Shutdown)
    18→
    19→```python
    20→from cohezion.compound.session_manager import CompoundSessionManager
    21→
    22→async with CompoundSessionManager() as mgr:
    23→    summary = mgr.start_session(max_cache_entries=256)
    24→    # ... compound cycles ...
    25→    result = mgr.end_session()
    26→```
    27→
    28→**Rules:**
    29→- Always use context manager for clean shutdown
    30→- `start_session()` loads warm cache and metrics snapshot
    31→- `end_session()` persists cache and saves metrics snapshot
    32→
    33→### Checkpoint Persistence
    34→
    35→| Storage | Primary | Fallback |
    36→|---------|---------|----------|
    37→| Checkpoints | Vault MCP (`mcp.vault_write`) | Local JSONL in `data/checkpoints/` |
    38→| Cache | Vault MCP | Local JSONL in `data/cache/` |
    39→
    40→**Pattern:**
    41→```python
    42→from cohezion.compound.cache_persistence import CachePersistence, WarmCacheLoader
    43→
    44→# On start: warm cache
    45→loader = WarmCacheLoader()
    46→entries_loaded = loader.warm_client(client, max_entries=256)
    47→
    48→# On end: persist cache
    49→cp = CachePersistence()
    50→cp.save_cache(client._cache)
    51→```
    52→
    53→### FLUME VAE (256D Latent Space)
    54→
    55→- **Location**: `src/cohezion/flume/`
    56→- **Architecture**: Encoder → 256D latent → Decoder
    57→- **Purpose**: Transform raw requests into manifold coordinates
    58→- **Integration**: Called in `CompoundExecutor` Step 3 (Manifest)
    59→
    60→### 12D Universe Journey Tracking
    61→
    62→```python
    63→from cohezion.compound.journey_tracker import JourneyTracker
    64→
    65→tracker = JourneyTracker()
    66→state = tracker.record_state(
    67→    agent_id="agent-1",
    68→    phase="execution",
    69→    position={"x": 0.5, "y": 0.3, "z": 0.7},  # 3D base
    70→    coherence=0.85,
    71→    # 9 additional dimensions auto-expanded
    72→)
    73→```
    74→
    75→**Dimensions**: x, y, z (spatial) + coherence + energy + entropy + momentum + phase + velocity + amplitude + frequency
    76→
    77→### Request Alignment Coherence Scoring
    78→
    79→```python
    80→from cohezion.compound.request_alignment_analyzer import RequestAlignmentAnalyzer
    81→
    82→analyzer = RequestAlignmentAnalyzer()
    83→alignment = analyzer.analyze(request, available_skills, agent_context)
    84→if alignment.coherence < 0.5:
    85→    logger.warning(f"Low alignment: {alignment.issues}")
    86→```
    87→
    88→**Threshold**: Coherence < 0.5 requires human review
    89→
    90→### Cost-Aware Model Routing
    91→
    92→```python
    93→from cohezion.swarm.cost_aware_router import CostAwareRouter
    94→
    95→router = CostAwareRouter()
    96→model = router.select_model(task_complexity=0.7, budget_remaining=0.50)
    97→```
    98→
    99→**Model Tiers**:
   100→| Tier | Use Case | Cost |
   101→|------|----------|------|
   102→| Local (Ollama) | Simple extraction, classification | $0 |
   103→| Cloud (Claude) | Complex reasoning, multi-step | $3-15/M tokens |
   104→
   105→---
   106→
   107→## Critical Implementation Rules
   108→
   109→### Async / I/O
   110→
   111→- **ALL** I/O must be `async/await` with timeouts
   112→- Never use blocking calls in async contexts
   113→- Global Ollama limit: 4 concurrent requests
   114→
   115→### Testing
   116→
   117→- **Mock at source**: `@patch("cohezion.module.function")` — NOT at consumer
   118→- **Singleton reset**: Reset in `tests/conftest.py` between tests
   119→- **Fixtures**: Use `mock_ollama`, `mock_surreal` for unit tests
   120→- **Markers**: `@pytest.mark.fast` (<1s, no live services)
   121→
   122→### Type Safety
   123→
   124→- Mandatory type hints on all public signatures
   125→- Use modern syntax: `list[int]`, `str | None`
   126→- mypy `--strict` compatible
   127→
   128→### Import Management
   129→
   130→- Standard library → Third-party → Local (`cohezion`)
   131→- Never use `ruff --unsafe-fixes` (breaks mock.patch targets)
   132→
   133→---
   134→
   135→## Project Structure
   136→
   137→```
   138→src/cohezion/
   139→├── compound/       # 11-step executor, skill refiner, retrospection
   140→├── swarm/          # Team orchestration, cost routing
   141→├── cache/          # L1/L2/L3 semantic cache
   142→├── flume/          # VAE encoder (256D latent)
   143→├── skills/         # PRIME skill definitions (*.md)
   144→├── api/            # FastAPI backend (72 endpoints)
   145→└── core/           # Persistence, repositories
   146→```
   147→
   148→---
   149→
   150→## Key Classes
   151→
   152→| Class | File | Purpose |
   153→|-------|------|---------|
   154→| `CompoundExecutor` | `compound/executor.py` | 11-step pipeline orchestrator |
   155→| `CompoundSessionManager` | `compound/session_manager.py` | Lifecycle management |
   156→| `JourneyTracker` | `compound/journey_tracker.py` | 12D state recording |
   157→| `RequestAlignmentAnalyzer` | `compound/request_alignment_analyzer.py` | Coherence scoring |
   158→| `CostAwareRouter` | `swarm/cost_aware_router.py` | Model selection |
   159→| `GlobalMetricsAggregator` | `compound/global_metrics_aggregator.py` | Metrics collection |
   160→
   161→---
   162→
   163→## Build Commands
   164→
   165→```bash
   166→make format        # ruff format
   167→make lint          # ruff check --fix
   168→make type-check    # mypy
   169→make test-fast     # pytest -m fast
   170→make test          # Full suite (~90s)
   171→```
   172→
   173→---
   174→
   175→## Anti-Patterns (Never Do)
   176→
   177→- Block I/O in async handlers
   178→- Mock after import (`@patch("cohezion.api.client")`)
   179→- Use bare `pip` instead of `uv`
   180→- Skip type hints "for speed"
   181→- Hardcode credentials (use Vault)

     8→# PRD Create Workflow
     9→
    10→**Goal:** Create comprehensive PRDs through structured workflow facilitation.
    11→
    12→**Your Role:** Product-focused PM facilitator collaborating with an expert peer.
    13→
    14→You will continue to operate with your given name, identity, and communication_style, merged with the details of this role description.
    15→
    16→## WORKFLOW ARCHITECTURE
    17→
    18→This uses **step-file architecture** for disciplined execution:
    19→
    20→### Core Principles
    21→
    22→- **Micro-file Design**: Each step is a self contained instruction file that is a part of an overall workflow that must be followed exactly
    23→- **Just-In-Time Loading**: Only the current step file is in memory - never load future step files until told to do so
    24→- **Sequential Enforcement**: Sequence within the step files must be completed in order, no skipping or optimization allowed
    25→- **State Tracking**: Document progress in output file frontmatter using `stepsCompleted` array when a workflow produces a document
    26→- **Append-Only Building**: Build documents by appending content as directed to the output file
    27→
    28→### Step Processing Rules
    29→
    30→1. **READ COMPLETELY**: Always read the entire step file before taking any action
    31→2. **FOLLOW SEQUENCE**: Execute all numbered sections in order, never deviate
    32→3. **WAIT FOR INPUT**: If a menu is presented, halt and wait for user selection
    33→4. **CHECK CONTINUATION**: If the step has a menu with Continue as an option, only proceed to next step when user selects 'C' (Continue)
    34→5. **SAVE STATE**: Update `stepsCompleted` in frontmatter before loading next step
    35→6. **LOAD NEXT**: When directed, read fully and follow the next step file
    36→
    37→### Critical Rules (NO EXCEPTIONS)

     1→# Cloud Vault MCP Server Integration
     2→
     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→The Cloud Vault MCP Server provides a Model Context Protocol (MCP) interface for cohezion's compound engineering system. It enables AI agents to read, write, search, and organize knowledge in a structured Obsidian vault, creating a persistent memory layer that accumulates reusable context across sessions.
     6→
     7→## Architecture
     8→
     9→```
    10→┌─────────────────┐         ┌──────────────────┐         ┌─────────────────┐
    11→│  Cohezion Core  │ ◄─────► │  MCP Server      │ ◄─────► │ Obsidian Vault  │
    12→│  (Client)       │  HTTP   │  (cloud-vault)   │  FS     │  (Git Repo)     │
    13→└─────────────────┘         └──────────────────┘         └─────────────────┘
    14→                                     │
    15→                                     ▼
    16→                            ┌─────────────────┐
    17→                            │   Git Sync      │
    18→                            │   (Optional)    │
    19→                            └─────────────────┘
    20→```
    21→
    22→The server provides three categories of operations:
    23→
    24→1. **Core Vault Operations**: Read, write, edit, delete, list, search
    25→2. **Obsidian-Aware Operations**: Backlinks, forward links, tags, templates
    26→3. **Compound Engineering Operations**: Log decisions, experiments, patterns; find context
    27→
    28→## Setup
    29→
    30→### Prerequisites
    31→
    32→- Python 3.11+
    33→- Docker and Docker Compose (for containerized deployment)
    34→- Git (vault is versioned)
    35→
    36→### Quick Start (Docker)
    37→
    38→1. **Clone and navigate to the MCP server directory**:
    39→   ```bash
    40→   cd /home/mike-anderson/dev/cohezion/cloud-vault-mcp
    41→   ```
    42→
    43→2. **Run the setup script**:
    44→   ```bash
    45→   ./setup.sh
    46→   ```
    47→
    48→   This script will:
    49→   - Create `.env` from `.env.example`
    50→   - Generate a secure API key (SHA-256 hash)
    51→   - Initialize the vault as a Git repository
    52→   - Build and start the Docker container
    53→
    54→3. **Save the API key** displayed during setup. You'll need it for client configuration.
    55→
    56→4. **Verify the server is running**:
    57→   ```bash
    58→   curl http://localhost:8360/health
    59→   ```
    60→
    61→   Expected response: `{"status":"ok"}`
    62→
    63→### Development Setup (Local Python)
    64→
    65→For local development without Docker:
    66→
    67→```bash
    68→cd /home/mike-anderson/dev/cohezion/cloud-vault-mcp
    69→./setup.sh --dev
    70→```
    71→
    72→Then start the server:
    73→
    74→```bash
    75→export VAULT_PATH=$(pwd)/vault
    76→source .env
    77→export MCP_API_KEY MCP_PORT
    78→cloud-vault-mcp
    79→```
    80→
    81→Or run directly:
    82→
    83→```bash
    84→VAULT_PATH=$(pwd)/vault \
    85→MCP_API_KEY=$(grep MCP_API_KEY .env | cut -d= -f2) \
    86→python -m mcp_server.main
    87→```
    88→
    89→### Configuration
    90→
    91→Edit `.env` to customize server settings:
    92→
    93→```bash
    94→# API key for authentication (required)
    95→MCP_API_KEY=<your-generated-key>
    96→
    97→# Server port (default: 8360)
    98→MCP_PORT=8360
    99→
   100→# Vault path (default: /vault in Docker, ./vault locally)
   101→VAULT_PATH=/vault
   102→
   103→# CORS allowed origins (default: *)
   104→CORS_ORIGINS=*
   105→
   106→# Log level (default: info)
   107→LOG_LEVEL=info
   108→
   109→# Git sync interval in seconds (default: 300 = 5 minutes)
   110→GIT_SYNC_INTERVAL=300
   111→
   112→# Optional: Git remote URL for vault backup
   113→GIT_REMOTE_URL=
   114→```
   115→
   116→## Client Configuration
   117→
   118→### Claude Code Integration
   119→
   120→Add the MCP server to your Claude Code configuration:
   121→
   122→**Option 1: Global config** (`~/.claude/mcp.json`):
   123→```json
   124→{
   125→  "mcpServers": {
   126→    "cloud-vault": {
   127→      "type": "streamable-http",
   128→      "url": "http://localhost:8360/mcp",
   129→      "headers": {
   130→        "Authorization": "Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>"
   131→      }
   132→    }
   133→  }
   134→}
   135→```
   136→
   137→**Option 2: Project-specific config** (`.mcp.json` in project root):
   138→```json
   139→{
   140→  "mcpServers": {
   141→    "cloud-vault": {
   142→      "type": "streamable-http",
   143→      "url": "http://localhost:8360/mcp",
   144→      "headers": {
   145→        "Authorization": "Bearer <YOUR_API_KEY>"
   146→      }
   147→    }
   148→  }
   149→}
   150→```
   151→
   152→Replace `<YOUR_API_KEY>` with the key generated during setup.
   153→
   154→### Cohezion Integration
   155→
   156→The cohezion core can connect to the MCP server through the `ContextEngineeringInfrastructure` class:
   157→
   158→```python
   159→from cohezion.core.context_engineering import ContextEngineeringInfrastructure
   160→import requests
   161→
   162→class VaultMCPClient:
   163→    """Client for Cloud Vault MCP Server."""
   164→
   165→    def __init__(self, base_url: str, api_key: str):
   166→        self.base_url = base_url.rstrip('/')
   167→        self.headers = {
   168→            'Authorization': f'Bearer {api_key}',
   169→            'Content-Type': 'application/json'
   170→        }
   171→
   172→    def call_tool(self, tool_name: str, **kwargs):
   173→        """Call an MCP tool by name."""
   174→        response = requests.post(
   175→            f'{self.base_url}/mcp/tools/call',
   176→            headers=self.headers,
   177→            json={'tool': tool_name, 'arguments': kwargs}
   178→        )
   179→        response.raise_for_status()
   180→        return response.json()
   181→
   182→    def vault_read(self, path: str) -> str:
   183→        """Read a note from the vault."""
   184→        return self.call_tool('vault_read', path=path)
   185→
   186→    def vault_write(self, path: str, content: str) -> str:
   187→        """Write a note to the vault."""
   188→        return self.call_tool('vault_write', path=path, content=content)
   189→
   190→    def vault_search(self, query: str, scope: str = 'all', folder: str = '') -> dict:
   191→        """Search the vault."""
   192→        return self.call_tool('vault_search', query=query, scope=scope, folder=folder)
   193→
   194→    def log_decision(self, project: str, title: str, context: str,
   195→                    decision: str, rationale: str,
   196→                    alternatives_considered: str = '') -> str:
   197→        """Log an architecture decision."""
   198→        return self.call_tool(
   199→            'vault_log_decision',
   200→            project=project,
   201→            title=title,
   202→            context=context,
   203→            decision=decision,
   204→            rationale=rationale,
   205→            alternatives_considered=alternatives_considered
   206→        )
   207→
   208→    def find_relevant_context(self, query: str, project: str = '') -> dict:
   209→        """Find relevant prior decisions, patterns, and experiments."""
   210→        return self.call_tool(
   211→            'vault_find_relevant_context',
   212→            query=query,
   213→            project=project
   214→        )
   215→
   216→# Wire into ContextEngineeringInfrastructure
   217→infra = ContextEngineeringInfrastructure()
   218→vault_client = VaultMCPClient(
   219→    base_url='http://localhost:8360',
   220→    api_key='<YOUR_API_KEY>'
   221→)
   222→
   223→infra.register_tool('vault_read', vault_client.vault_read)
   224→infra.register_tool('vault_write', vault_client.vault_write)
   225→infra.register_tool('vault_search', vault_client.vault_search)
   226→infra.register_tool('log_decision', vault_client.log_decision)
   227→infra.register_tool('find_context', vault_client.find_relevant_context)
   228→```
   229→
   230→## Usage Examples
   231→
   232→### Example 1: Log an Architecture Decision
   233→
   234→```python
   235→vault_client = VaultMCPClient('http://localhost:8360', api_key)
   236→
   237→result = vault_client.log_decision(
   238→    project='cohezion',
   239→    title='Use FastMCP for MCP Server Framework',
   240→    context='Need to build an MCP server for Cloud Vault. FastMCP provides a high-level API over the MCP SDK.',
   241→    decision='Use FastMCP library to implement the MCP server',
   242→    rationale='FastMCP reduces boilerplate, provides decorator-based tool registration, and handles streaming HTTP automatically.',
   243→    alternatives_considered='Raw MCP SDK (more complex), custom HTTP wrapper (reinventing the wheel)'
   244→)
   245→
   246→print(result)
   247→# Output: "Created decision: decisions/cohezion/2026-02-07-use-fastmcp-for-mcp-server-framework.md"
   248→```
   249→
   250→### Example 2: Search for Prior Context
   251→
   252→Before implementing a new feature, search for relevant past decisions and patterns:
   253→
   254→```python
   255→# Find decisions about MCP integration
   256→results = vault_client.find_relevant_context(
   257→    query='MCP integration authentication',
   258→    project='cohezion'
   259→)
   260→
   261→print(results)
   262→# Returns JSON with matching decisions, patterns, experiments, and concepts
   263→```
   264→
   265→### Example 3: Log an Experiment
   266→

   343→
   344→## Available MCP Tools
   345→
   346→### Core Vault Operations
   347→
   348→- `vault_read(path: str)` - Read a note's content
   349→- `vault_write(path: str, content: str)` - Create or overwrite a note
   350→- `vault_edit(path: str, edits: list[dict])` - Apply surgical edits
   351→- `vault_delete(path: str)` - Delete a note
   352→- `vault_list(directory: str = "", recursive: bool = False)` - List contents
   353→- `vault_search(query: str, scope: str = "all", folder: str = "")` - Full-text search
   354→
   355→### Obsidian-Aware Operations
   356→
   357→- `vault_backlinks(path: str)` - Find notes linking TO this note
   358→- `vault_forward_links(path: str)` - Find notes this note links TO
   359→- `vault_tags(path: str = "")` - List tags (vault-wide or for a note)
   360→- `vault_create_from_template(template_name: str, target_path: str, variables: dict)` - Create from template
   361→
   362→### Compound Engineering Operations
   363→
   364→- `vault_log_decision(...)` - Create an Architecture Decision Record (ADR)
   365→- `vault_log_experiment(...)` - Log hypothesis, method, results, learnings
   366→- `vault_extract_pattern(...)` - Extract a reusable pattern
   367→- `vault_find_relevant_context(query: str, project: str = "")` - Search decisions, patterns, experiments
   368→
   369→## Vault Structure
   370→
   371→The vault organizes notes into semantic directories:
   372→
   373→```
   374→vault/
   375→├── projects/        # Per-project documentation and index notes
   376→├── decisions/       # Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)
   377→├── patterns/        # Reusable solutions extracted from projects
   378→├── experiments/     # Hypothesis, method, results, learnings
   379→├── papers/          # Literature notes from arXiv and other sources
   380→├── daily/           # Daily development logs
   381→├── concepts/        # Evergreen notes on technical concepts
   382→├── tools/           # Notes on tools, configurations, environments
   383→└── inbox/           # Quick capture, unsorted notes
   384→```
   385→
   386→Each directory contains a `_template.md` for structured note creation.
   387→
   388→## Troubleshooting
   389→
   390→### Server Won't Start
   391→
   392→**Problem**: `docker compose up` fails or server doesn't respond.
   393→
   394→**Solutions**:
   395→1. Check if port 8360 is already in use:
   396→   ```bash
   397→   lsof -i :8360
   398→   ```
   399→   Change `MCP_PORT` in `.env` if needed.
   400→
   401→2. Check logs:
   402→   ```bash
   403→   docker logs cloud-vault-mcp
   404→   ```
   405→
   406→3. Verify Docker is running:
   407→   ```bash
   408→   docker ps
   409→   ```
   410→
   411→### Authentication Failures
   412→
   413→**Problem**: Client receives 401 Unauthorized.
   414→
   415→**Solutions**:
   416→1. Verify API key is correct:
   417→   ```bash
   418→   grep MCP_API_KEY .env
   419→   ```
   420→
   421→2. Check Authorization header format:
   422→   ```
   423→   Authorization: Bearer <key>
   424→   ```
   425→   NOT `Token <key>` or just `<key>`.
   426→
   427→3. Regenerate API key if needed:
   428→   ```bash
   429→   python3 -c "import hashlib, os; print(hashlib.sha256(os.urandom(32)).hexdigest())"
   430→   ```
   431→   Update `.env` and restart server.
   432→
   433→### Vault File Permission Issues
   434→
   435→**Problem**: Server can't read/write vault files.
   436→
   437→**Solutions**:
   438→1. Check vault directory ownership:
   439→   ```bash
   440→   ls -la cloud-vault-mcp/vault
   441→   ```
   442→
   443→2. For Docker deployment, ensure volume has correct permissions:
   444→   ```bash
   445→   docker exec cloud-vault-mcp ls -la /vault
   446→   ```
   447→
   448→3. For local development, ensure `VAULT_PATH` is writable:
   449→   ```bash
   450→   touch $VAULT_PATH/test.md && rm $VAULT_PATH/test.md
   451→   ```
   452→
   453→### Git Sync Not Working
   454→
   455→**Problem**: Changes aren't being committed or pushed.
   456→
   457→**Solutions**:
   458→1. Check git-sync container logs:
   459→   ```bash
   460→   docker logs cloud-vault-git-sync
   461→   ```
   462→
   463→2. Verify vault is a Git repo:
   464→   ```bash
   465→   cd cloud-vault-mcp/vault && git status
   466→   ```
   467→
   468→3. If using remote sync, verify `GIT_REMOTE_URL` is set in `.env`.
   469→
   470→4. Check Git credentials are configured:
   471→   ```bash
   472→   docker exec cloud-vault-git-sync git config --list
   473→   ```
   474→
   475→### MCP Tools Not Appearing in Claude Code
   476→
   477→**Problem**: Claude Code doesn't see the MCP server's tools.
   478→
   479→**Solutions**:
   480→1. Verify MCP config location:
   481→   - Global: `~/.claude/mcp.json`
   482→   - Project: `.mcp.json` in project root
   483→
   484→2. Check JSON syntax is valid:
   485→   ```bash
   486→   python3 -m json.tool ~/.claude/mcp.json
   487→   ```
   488→
   489→3. Restart Claude Code after config changes.
   490→
   491→4. Test MCP endpoint directly:
   492→   ```bash
   493→   curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" \
   494→        http://localhost:8360/mcp/tools/list
   495→   ```
   496→
   497→### Connection Timeouts
   498→
   499→**Problem**: Client requests hang or timeout.
   500→
   501→**Solutions**:
   502→1. Check server is reachable:
   503→   ```bash
   504→   curl -I http://localhost:8360/health
   505→   ```
   506→
   507→2. For Docker, verify container is running:
   508→   ```bash
   509→   docker ps | grep cloud-vault
   510→   ```
   511→
   512→3. Check firewall/network settings if connecting from external host.
   513→
   514→4. Increase client timeout if processing large vault operations.
   515→
   516→## Security Considerations
   517→
   518→### API Key Management
   519→
   520→1. **Never commit API keys to Git**:
   521→   - `.env` is in `.gitignore`
   522→   - Use environment variables for client configuration
   523→
   524→2. **Rotate keys periodically**:
   525→   - Generate new key with provided Python command
   526→   - Update `.env` and client configs
   527→   - Restart server
   528→
   529→3. **Use secure key generation**:
   530→   ```bash
   531→   python3 -c "import hashlib, os; print(hashlib.sha256(os.urandom(32)).hexdigest())"
   532→   ```
   533→   Don't use weak passwords or predictable values.
   534→
   535→### Network Security
   536→
   537→1. **Use HTTPS in production**:
   538→   - Configure nginx with TLS certificates
   539→   - Store certs in `deploy/nginx/certs/`
   540→   - Start nginx: `docker compose up -d nginx`
   541→
   542→2. **Restrict CORS origins**:
   543→   ```bash
   544→   # In .env
   545→   CORS_ORIGINS=https://your-claude-instance.com,https://trusted-client.com
   546→   ```
   547→
   548→3. **Use firewall rules**:
   549→   - Only expose port 8360 (or 443 for nginx) to trusted networks
   550→   - For local development, bind to `127.0.0.1` only
   551→
   552→### Vault Content Security
   553→
   554→1. **Sensitive data in vault**:
   555→   - Avoid storing credentials, API keys, or secrets in vault notes
   556→   - Use `.gitignore` patterns for sensitive files
   557→   - Consider encrypting sensitive notes with git-crypt
   558→
   559→2. **Git remote authentication**:
   560→   - Use SSH keys for Git remote URL
   561→   - Don't embed credentials in `GIT_REMOTE_URL`
   562→   - Configure Git credential store separately
   563→
   564→3. **Docker volume permissions**:
   565→   - Vault data volume is persistent across container restarts
   566→   - Backup vault data regularly:
   567→     ```bash
   568→     docker run --rm -v cloud-vault-mcp_vault-data:/vault -v $(pwd)/backup:/backup alpine tar czf /backup/vault-backup.tar.gz /vault
   569→     ```
   570→
   571→## Advanced Usage
   572→
   573→### Custom Templates
   574→
   575→Add custom templates to vault directories:
   576→
   577→1. Create `vault/<category>/_template.md`
   578→2. Use `{{variable}}` syntax for placeholders
   579→3. Call `vault_create_from_template` with template name and variables
   580→
   581→### Git Integration
   582→
   583→The vault is a Git repository. All changes are tracked:
   584→
   585→```bash
   586→# View commit history
   587→cd cloud-vault-mcp/vault
   588→git log --oneline
   589→
   590→# Manual commit
   591→git add -A
   592→git commit -m "Manual update"
   593→
   594→# Push to remote
   595→git push origin main
   596→```
   597→
   598→Auto-sync commits every 5 minutes (configurable via `GIT_SYNC_INTERVAL`).
   599→
   600→### Obsidian Desktop Integration
   601→
   602→Open the vault in Obsidian for visual editing:
   603→
   604→1. Open Obsidian
   605→2. "Open folder as vault"
   606→3. Select `cloud-vault-mcp/vault/`
   607→4. Changes sync via Git (pull before editing, commit after)
   608→
   609→### Scaling and Performance
   610→
   611→For large vaults (>10,000 notes):
   612→
   613→1. **Use folder-scoped search**:
   614→   ```python
   615→   vault_client.vault_search(query='term', scope='folder', folder='decisions')
   616→   ```
   617→
   618→2. **Enable Git shallow clones** for faster sync:
   619→   ```bash
   620→   git clone --depth 1 <remote_url>
   621→   ```
   622→
   623→3. **Consider separate vaults per project**:
   624→   - Run multiple MCP servers on different ports
   625→   - Each with its own vault and API key
   626→
   627→4. **Use indexing for full-text search** (future enhancement):
   628→   - Whoosh or Elasticsearch integration
   629→   - Pre-build search index for faster queries
   630→

    80→
    81→## Python-Specific Rules
    82→
    83→### Async / I/O (Critical)
    84→
    85→- **ALL** I/O must be `async/await` with timeouts
    86→- Never use blocking calls in async contexts
    87→- `asyncio.Lock()` and `asyncio.Semaphore()` in `__init__`, **never class-level** (stale event loop in pytest)
    88→- `asyncio.run()` conflict: use thread pool offloading when called from existing event loop:
    89→
    90→```python
    91→try:
    92→    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    93→except RuntimeError:
    94→    return asyncio.run(async_func(*args))
    95→with ThreadPoolExecutor() as executor:
    96→    future = executor.submit(lambda: asyncio.run(async_func(*args)))
    97→    return future.result()
    98→```
    99→
   100→- Track all `asyncio.create_task()` results in a `set` to prevent GC mid-execution
   101→- Explicit `asyncio.wait_for()` timeout on long-running subprocesses
   102→
   103→### Import Management
   104→
   105→- Order: Standard library → Third-party → Local (`cohezion`)
   106→- Never use `ruff --unsafe-fixes` (TC001/TC002/TC003 moves imports to TYPE_CHECKING, breaking `patch()` calls in tests)
   107→- Remove unused imports immediately
   108→
   109→### Type Safety
   110→
   111→- Mandatory type hints on all public signatures
   112→- Use modern syntax: `list[int]`, `str | None` (not `Optional[int]`)
   113→- mypy `--strict` compatible target
   114→- `check_untyped_defs = true` in pyproject.toml

   286→
   287→### Security Rules
   288→
   289→- **Never** print, echo, or display passwords or secrets
   290→- **Never** store `SUDO_PASSWORD` in `.env` — use passwordless sudo
   291→- **Never** write secrets to temp files that persist
   292→- **Never** use `git add -f` to stage gitignored files
   293→- Path validation: prevent directory traversal with symlink resolution
   294→- Use `python-jose` for JWT, `passlib[bcrypt]` for passwords

   297→
   298→## Compound Engineering Patterns
   299→
   300→### Session Lifecycle (Warm-Start / Clean-Shutdown)
   301→
   302→```python
   303→async with CompoundSessionManager() as mgr:
   304→    summary = mgr.start_session(max_cache_entries=256)
   305→    result = mgr.end_session()
   306→```
   307→
   308→### 11-Step Execution Pipeline
   309→
   310→```
   311→CompoundExecutor → RequestAlignmentAnalyzer → GlobalMetricsAggregator
   312→                → DegradationDetector → JourneyTracker → RetrospectionEngine
   313→                → SkillRefiner → SkillConsensusVoter → Updated Skill
   314→```
   315→
   316→### Key Thresholds
   317→
   318→- **HIHO Coherence**: 50% — optimal exploitation/exploration balance
   319→- **Request Alignment**: Coherence < 0.5 requires human review
   320→- **Predictive Throttling**: velocity gradient on 12D position (not reactive thresholds)
   321→
   322→### Checkpoint Persistence
   323→
   324→| Storage | Primary | Fallback |
   325→|---------|---------|----------|
   326→| Checkpoints | Vault MCP | Local JSONL `data/checkpoints/` |
   327→| Cache | Vault MCP | Local JSONL `data/cache/` |

   331→## Development Workflow
   332→
   333→### Package Management
   334→
   335→- **Always `uv`** — never bare `pip` or `pip install`
   336→- `uv sync` for dependencies, `uv run` for execution
   337→- Post-crash recovery: `uv add pytest pytest-cov pytest-asyncio --dev`

   339→### Build Commands
   340→

   343→make lint          # ruff check --fix
   344→make lint-check    # ruff check (no fix)
   345→make type-check    # mypy
   346→make test-fast     # pytest -m fast
   347→make test          # Full suite
   348→make all           # format + lint + type-check + test
   349→make ci            # Full CI pipeline
   350→```
   351→
   352→### Git Workflow
   353→
   354→- **Worktree sessions**: every Claude session in isolated worktree
   355→- Branch naming: `session-{N}-{type}` or `feature/`, `fix/`, `security/`
   356→- Conventional commits: `feat:`, `fix:`, `test:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`
   357→- AI commits include: `Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`
   358→- Never force-push to main/develop
   359→- No files >1MB (use git-lfs)
   360→
   361→### MCP Public Endpoint
   362→
   363→- `https://frameworkdesktop.tail54eb71.ts.net/mcp` via Tailscale Funnel
   364→- ISP blocks inbound 443; Tailscale uses outbound relay

   437→## Anti-Patterns (Never Do)
   438→
   439→- Block I/O in async handlers
   440→- Mock after import (`@patch("cohezion.api.client")`) — mock at source
   441→- Use bare `pip` instead of `uv`
   442→- Skip type hints "for speed"
   443→- Hardcode credentials (use Vault)
   444→- Use `ruff --unsafe-fixes` (breaks test patching)
   445→- Put `asyncio.Lock()` at class level (stale event loop)
   446→- Run tests without conftest singleton resets
   447→- Assume NVIDIA/CUDA (AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ only)
   448→- Use `asyncio.run()` inside existing event loop (thread pool instead)
   449→- Write infrastructure for products that don't exist
   450→- Write 600 pre-implementation tests (implement ONE feature, validate, write 5 tests)
   451→- Print/echo secrets or store `SUDO_PASSWORD` in `.env`
   452→- Force-add gitignored files (`git add -f`)
   453→- Run `ruff --unsafe-fixes` (TC001-3 breaks runtime patching)

     1→# MCP Server Configuration & Deployment
     2→
     3→Complete guide for configuring, deploying, and managing the Kyutai MCP Server.
     4→
     5→## Table of Contents
     6→
     7→1. [Server Overview](#server-overview)
     8→2. [Architecture](#architecture)
     9→3. [Configuration Options](#configuration-options)
    10→4. [Starting the Server](#starting-the-server)
    11→5. [Model Management](#model-management)
    12→6. [Health Checks & Monitoring](#health-checks--monitoring)
    13→7. [Performance Tuning](#performance-tuning)

    18→---
    19→
    20→## Server Overview
    21→
    22→The Kyutai MCP Server is a Python/FastAPI application that:
    23→- Exposes Kyutai voice AI tools via the Model Context Protocol (MCP)
    24→- Handles model loading, inference, and streaming
    25→- Provides REST/WebSocket endpoints for voice operations
    26→- Manages GPU/CPU resource allocation
    27→- Monitors health and performance
    28→
    29→**Technology Stack:**
    30→- Framework: FastAPI + Uvicorn
    31→- MCP Library: python-mcp
    32→- GPU: CUDA (NVIDIA), ROCm (AMD), MLX (Apple Silicon)
    33→- Async: asyncio, websockets
    34→- Monitoring: Prometheus metrics (optional)
    35→
    36→---
    37→
    38→## Architecture
    39→
    40→### System Components
    41→
    42→```
    43→┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
    44→│      Obsidian Plugin (Client)       │
    45→└─────────────────────────────────────┘
    46→              ↓ MCP Protocol
    47→┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
    48→│      MCP Server (FastAPI)           │
    49→│  ┌─────────────────────────────────┐│
    50→│  │  Tool Registry (7 tools)        ││
    51→│  ├─────────────────────────────────┤│
    52→│  │  Model Manager                  ││
    53→│  │  ├─ Pocket TTS                  ││
    54→│  │  ├─ Delayed Streams STT         ││
    55→│  │  ├─ Moshi                       ││
    56→│  │  └─ Community APIs              ││
    57→│  ├─────────────────────────────────┤│
    58→│  │  Audio Pipeline                 ││
    59→│  │  ├─ Input Stream Handler        ││
    60→│  │  ├─ Inference Engine            ││
    61→│  │  └─ Output Formatter            ││
    62→│  ├─────────────────────────────────┤│
    63→│  │  GPU/Resource Manager           ││
    64→│  │  ├─ Memory Allocation           ││
    65→│  │  ├─ Thread Pool                 ││
    66→│  │  └─ Error Recovery              ││
    67→│  └─────────────────────────────────┘│
    68→└─────────────────────────────────────┘
    69→         ↓ Local/GPU Hardware
    70→┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
    71→│   Kyutai Models (PyTorch/MLX)       │
    72→└─────────────────────────────────────┘
    73→```
    74→
    75→### Tool Registry
    76→
    77→The server exposes 7 MCP tools:
    78→
    79→| Tool | Purpose | Input | Output |
    80→|------|---------|-------|--------|
    81→| `synthesize_text` | Text-to-Speech | text, voice | audio binary |
    82→| `transcribe_audio` | Speech-to-Text | audio binary | text + timestamps |
    83→| `clone_voice` | Voice Profile | reference audio | voice state |
    84→| `list_voices` | Available Voices | — | voice list |
    85→| `list_models` | Available Models | — | model metadata |
    86→| `get_status` | Server Status | — | health metrics |
    87→| `stream_audio` | Real-time Streaming | audio stream | text stream |
    88→

    90→
    91→## Configuration Options
    92→
    93→### Environment Variables
    94→
    95→Create `.env` file with:
    96→
    97→```bash
    98→# ========== SERVER SETTINGS ==========
    99→MCP_HOST=127.0.0.1              # Bind address
   100→MCP_PORT=8000                   # Bind port
   101→MCP_LOG_LEVEL=INFO              # DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR
   102→MCP_WORKERS=4                   # Worker processes
   103→MCP_TIMEOUT=300                 # Request timeout (seconds)
   104→
   105→# ========== MODEL SELECTION ==========
   106→TTS_PROVIDER=pocket-tts         # pocket-tts, moshi, community-api
   107→STT_PROVIDER=stt-1b-en_fr       # stt-1b, stt-2.6b, community-api
   108→STT_LANGUAGE=en_fr              # en_fr, en (depends on model)
   109→
   110→# ========== GPU CONFIGURATION ==========
   111→USE_GPU=true                    # Enable GPU acceleration
   112→GPU_DEVICE=auto                 # auto, cuda:0, cuda:1, mps, cpu
   113→CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0          # GPU IDs to use (0,1,2,...)
   114→GPU_MEMORY_FRACTION=0.8         # GPU memory limit (0.0-1.0)
   115→GPU_MEMORY_GROWTH=true          # Dynamic memory allocation
   116→
   117→# ========== QUANTIZATION ==========
   118→QUANTIZE_MODELS=false           # 4-bit/8-bit quantization
   119→QUANTIZATION_BITS=8             # 4 or 8
   120→MODEL_CACHE_DIR=~/.cache/huggingface  # Model cache location
   121→
   122→# ========== HUGGING FACE ==========
   123→HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN=hf_xxx   # Required for gated models
   124→HF_CACHE_DIR=~/.cache/huggingface
   125→HF_DATASETS_OFFLINE=false
   126→
   127→# ========== AUDIO SETTINGS ==========
   128→SAMPLE_RATE=24000               # Audio sample rate (Hz)
   129→CHUNK_SIZE=1024                 # Processing chunk size
   130→CHANNELS=1                      # Mono (1) or Stereo (2)
   131→BIT_DEPTH=16                    # 16 or 32-bit
   132→
   133→# ========== COMMUNITY API ENDPOINTS ==========
   134→COMMUNITY_TTS_URL=http://localhost:8001/v1
   135→COMMUNITY_STT_URL=http://localhost:8002/v1
   136→
   137→# ========== MONITORING ==========
   138→ENABLE_METRICS=true             # Prometheus metrics
   139→METRICS_PORT=9090               # Prometheus port
   140→HEALTH_CHECK_INTERVAL=30        # Health check interval (seconds)
   141→
   142→# ========== LOGGING ==========
   143→LOG_DIR=./logs
   144→LOG_MAX_SIZE=100MB
   145→LOG_BACKUP_COUNT=10
   146→LOG_FORMAT=json                 # json or text

   288→
   289→**Create `/etc/systemd/system/kyutai-mcp.service`:**

   291→[Unit]

   317→
   318→## Model Management
   319→
   320→### Preloading Models
   321→
   322→Models are lazily loaded on first use. To preload:
   323→
   324→```python
   325→from kyutai_mcp import MCPServer
   326→
   327→server = MCPServer()
   328→server.preload_models()  # Load all configured models
   329→server.start()
   330→```
   331→
   332→**Via CLI:**
   333→```bash
   334→python -m kyutai_mcp.server --preload-models
   335→```
   336→
   337→### Model Caching
   338→
   339→Models are cached in `~/.cache/huggingface`:
   340→
   341→```bash
   342→# View cache
   343→ls ~/.cache/huggingface/hub/
   344→
   345→# Clear cache (removes all models)
   346→rm -rf ~/.cache/huggingface/hub/
   347→
   348→# Set custom cache dir
   349→export HF_HOME=/mnt/large_ssd/models
   350→```

   484→## Performance Tuning
   485→
   486→### Optimize for Latency
   487→
   488→**Goal: Minimal response time**
   489→
   490→```bash
   491→# .env configuration
   492→USE_GPU=true
   493→GPU_DEVICE=cuda:0
   494→GPU_MEMORY_FRACTION=1.0          # Use full GPU
   495→QUANTIZE_MODELS=false             # Higher precision = higher latency
   496→MCP_WORKERS=8                      # More workers
   497→TTS_PROVIDER=pocket-tts            # Fastest provider
   498→STT_PROVIDER=stt-1b-en_fr         # Faster than 2.6B
   499→SAMPLE_RATE=16000                 # Lower sample rate
   500→CHUNK_SIZE=512                    # Smaller chunks
   501→```
   502→
   503→**Expected latency:**
   504→- Voice synthesis: 50-100ms
   505→- Speech transcription: 160-200ms
   506→
   507→### Optimize for Throughput
   508→
   509→**Goal: Maximum concurrent requests**
   510→
   511→```bash
   512→# .env configuration
   513→USE_GPU=true
   514→GPU_DEVICE=cuda:0
   515→QUANTIZE_MODELS=true              # 8-bit quantization
   516→MCP_WORKERS=16                     # Many workers
   517→GPU_MEMORY_FRACTION=0.9            # Leave headroom
   518→CHUNK_SIZE=2048                    # Larger chunks
   519→```
   520→
   521→**Expected throughput:**
   522→- Pocket TTS: 10+ concurrent
   523→- STT 1B: 64 concurrent streams
   524→- STT 2.6B: 32 concurrent streams
   525→
   526→### Optimize for Memory
   527→
   528→**Goal: Minimal GPU memory usage**
   529→
   530→```bash
   531→# .env configuration
   532→USE_GPU=true
   533→QUANTIZE_MODELS=true              # 4-bit quantization
   534→GPU_MEMORY_FRACTION=0.5            # Conservative allocation
   535→CHUNK_SIZE=512
   536→TTS_PROVIDER=pocket-tts            # Smallest model
   537→STT_PROVIDER=stt-1b-en_fr
   538→```
   539→
   540→**Memory requirements:**
   541→- Pocket TTS: ~500MB
   542→- STT 1B: ~2.5GB
   543→- STT 2.6B: ~6GB
   544→- Total: ~9GB

   709→
   710→## Production Deployment
   711→
   712→### Pre-Deployment Checklist
   713→
   714→- [ ] Test all MCP tools with sample data
   715→- [ ] Verify GPU/CPU performance baselines
   716→- [ ] Configure monitoring (health checks, metrics)
   717→- [ ] Set up log aggregation
   718→- [ ] Configure resource limits
   719→- [ ] Test failover procedures
   720→- [ ] Document runbook
   721→
   722→### Deployment Architectures
   723→
   724→#### Option 1: Single Machine
   725→
   726→```
   727→┌──────────────────┐
   728→│  Obsidian + MCP  │
   729→│  (Same machine)  │
   730→└──────────────────┘
   731→```
   732→
   733→**Setup:**
   734→```bash
   735→python -m kyutai_mcp.server --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
   736→```
   737→
   738→**Pros:** Simple, lowest latency
   739→**Cons:** Resource contention, no redundancy
   740→
   741→#### Option 2: Separate Server
   742→
   743→```
   744→┌────────────────┐           ┌──────────────────┐
   745→│  Obsidian PC   │-----------|  MCP Server      |
   746→│                │  HTTP/WS  │  (Linux/GPU)     │
   747→└────────────────┘           └──────────────────┘
   748→```
   749→
   750→**Setup:**
   751→```bash
   752→# On GPU server
   753→python -m kyutai_mcp.server --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
   754→
   755→# Configure Obsidian to connect to remote server
   756→# Settings → Kyutai MCP → MCP Server URL: http://gpu-server:8000
   757→```
   758→
   759→**Pros:** Better resource isolation, dedicated GPU
   760→**Cons:** Network latency (~50-100ms), firewall needed
   761→
   762→#### Option 3: Kubernetes
   763→
   764→**Deployment file (`k8s-deployment.yaml`):**
   765→```yaml
   766→apiVersion: apps/v1
   767→kind: Deployment
   768→metadata:
   769→  name: kyutai-mcp
   770→spec:
   771→  replicas: 3
   772→  selector:
   773→    matchLabels:
   774→      app: kyutai-mcp
   775→  template:
   776→    metadata:
   777→      labels:
   778→        app: kyutai-mcp
   779→    spec:
   780→      containers:
   781→      - name: mcp-server
   782→        image: kyutai-mcp:latest
   783→        ports:
   784→        - containerPort: 8000
   785→        resources:
   786→          requests:
   787→            memory: "8Gi"
   788→            nvidia.com/gpu: "1"
   789→          limits:
   790→            memory: "16Gi"
   791→            nvidia.com/gpu: "1"
   792→        env:
   793→        - name: HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN
   794→          valueFrom:
   795→            secretKeyRef:
   796→              name: huggingface-token
   797→              key: token
   798→        livenessProbe:
   799→          httpGet:
   800→            path: /health
   801→            port: 8000
   802→          initialDelaySeconds: 30
   803→          periodSeconds: 10
   804→```
   805→
   806→**Deploy:**
   807→```bash
   808→kubectl apply -f k8s-deployment.yaml
   809→kubectl get pods -l app=kyutai-mcp
   810→```
   811→
   812→### Production Environment Variables
   813→
   814→```bash
   815→# Security
   816→HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN=<secure-token>    # Use secrets manager
   817→MCP_SECRET_KEY=<random-32-char-string>
   818→
   819→# Performance
   820→MCP_WORKERS=8
   821→GPU_MEMORY_FRACTION=0.9
   822→QUANTIZE_MODELS=true
   823→
   824→# Monitoring
   825→ENABLE_METRICS=true
   826→LOG_LEVEL=INFO
   827→LOG_FORMAT=json
   828→
   829→# Network
   830→MCP_HOST=0.0.0.0                         # Accept remote connections
   831→MCP_PORT=8000
   832→MCP_CORS_ORIGINS=https://example.com    # Restrict origins
   833→
   834→# Resource limits
   835→MCP_MAX_CONTENT_SIZE=52428800             # 50MB
   836→MCP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=300                   # 5 minutes
   837→```
   838→
   839→### Reverse Proxy (Nginx)
   840→
   841→**`/etc/nginx/sites-available/kyutai-mcp`:**
   842→```nginx
   843→upstream kyutai_mcp {
   844→    server localhost:8000;
   845→}
   846→
   847→server {
   848→    listen 443 ssl http2;
   849→    server_name mcp.example.com;
   850→
   851→    ssl_certificate /etc/letsencrypt/live/mcp.example.com/fullchain.pem;
   852→    ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/mcp.example.com/privkey.pem;
   853→
   854→    client_max_body_size 50M;
   855→
   856→    location / {
   857→        proxy_pass http://kyutai_mcp;
   858→        proxy_set_header Host $host;
   859→        proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
   860→        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
   861→        proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
   862→
   863→        # WebSocket support
   864→        proxy_http_version 1.1;
   865→        proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
   866→        proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
   867→
   868→        # Timeouts for long-running inference
   869→        proxy_connect_timeout 300s;
   870→        proxy_send_timeout 300s;
   871→        proxy_read_timeout 300s;
   872→    }
   873→
   874→    # Rate limiting
   875→    limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=mcp_limit:10m rate=10r/s;
   876→    limit_req zone=mcp_limit burst=20 nodelay;
   877→}
   878→```
   879→
   880→### Load Balancing
   881→
   882→**Multiple server instances:**
   883→```nginx
   884→upstream kyutai_mcp {
   885→    least_conn;  # Route to least busy server
   886→    server gpu-server-1:8000;
   887→    server gpu-server-2:8000;
   888→    server gpu-server-3:8000;
   889→}
   890→```
   891→
   892→### Monitoring in Production
   893→
   894→**Prometheus scrape config:**
   895→```yaml
   896→scrape_configs:
   897→  - job_name: 'kyutai-mcp'
   898→    static_configs:
   899→      - targets: ['localhost:9090']
   900→    scrape_interval: 15s
   901→```
   902→
   903→**Alerting rules (`alerts.yml`):**
   904→```yaml
   905→- alert: KyutaiMCPDown
   906→  expr: up{job="kyutai-mcp"} == 0
   907→  for: 1m
   908→  annotations:
   909→    summary: "Kyutai MCP Server Down"
   910→
   911→- alert: HighGPUMemory
   912→  expr: kyutai_gpu_memory_bytes > 0.9 * kyutai_gpu_memory_total_bytes
   913→  annotations:
   914→    summary: "GPU Memory Usage High"
   915→
   916→- alert: HighErrorRate
   917→  expr: rate(kyutai_errors_total[5m]) > 0.05
   918→  annotations:
   919→    summary: "Error Rate > 5%"
   920→```

    23→    23→## Research Overview
    24→    24→
    25→    25→This technical research investigates how Cohezion's vault MCP server can be improved by leveraging Obsidian's full capability set and integrating with BMAD workflow artifacts (PRDs, Architecture Decisions, Epics, and Stories). The research covers the Obsidian platform ecosystem (Properties, Canvas, Dataview, Templater), the MCP protocol's three primitives (Tools, Resources, Prompts), 24+ existing Obsidian MCP server implementations, and our own 47-tool vault MCP server architecture.
    26→    26→
    27→    27→Key findings: Our vault MCP server has a critical integration gap — no connection between BMAD workflow artifacts and vault knowledge. We only use MCP Tools, missing Resources (browsable vault structure) and Prompts (reusable workflow templates). A 4-phase implementation roadmap (6-10 days) can bridge this gap with 8 new tools, 6 new resources, and 4 new prompts, requiring zero new infrastructure. See the full Executive Summary and Strategic Recommendations in the Research Synthesis section below.
    28→    28→

    53→    53→## Technology Stack Analysis
    54→    54→
    55→    55→### Obsidian Core Platform
    56→    56→
    57→    57→Obsidian is a local-first, Markdown-based knowledge management tool with an extensible plugin architecture. It stores all data as plain `.md` files on disk, making it fully interoperable with any tool that reads Markdown. As of 2025-2026, Obsidian has matured into a comprehensive PKM (Personal Knowledge Management) platform used at scale — one practitioner documented 8,000 notes with 64,000+ internal links managed over 3+ years.
    58→    58→
    59→    59→_Core Architecture: Local-first markdown files, YAML frontmatter metadata, wiki-link graph, plugin extensibility_
    60→    60→_Current Version: 1.9+ with Properties system, Canvas, and Bases (database views)_
    61→    61→_Strengths: Zero vendor lock-in, offline-first, plain-text portability, massive plugin ecosystem_
    62→    62→_Source: [Obsidian Help](https://help.obsidian.md/properties), [PKM at Scale](https://www.dsebastien.net/personal-knowledge-management-at-scale-analyzing-8-000-notes-and-64-000-links/)_
    63→    63→
    64→    64→### Properties & Metadata System (YAML Frontmatter)
    65→    65→
    66→    66→Obsidian supports 7 property types: **Text**, **List**, **Number**, **Checkbox**, **Date**, **Date & Time**, and **Tags**. Properties are stored as YAML frontmatter and enforced vault-wide — once a property name is assigned a type, ALL notes with that property must use the same type.
    67→    67→
    68→    68→_Supported Types: text, list, number, checkbox, date, datetime, tags_
    69→    69→_Default Properties: `tags` (hierarchical), `aliases` (search), `cssclasses` (styling)_
    70→    70→_Limitation: No nested YAML support in visual editor (Source mode only for complex structures)_
    71→    71→_Vault-Wide Enforcement: Property type is consistent across entire vault_
    72→    72→_Source: [Obsidian Properties](https://help.obsidian.md/properties), [DeepWiki Properties](https://deepwiki.com/obsidianmd/obsidian-help/4.3-properties-and-metadata)_
    73→    73→
    74→    74→### Canvas System (JSON-Based Visual Workspace)
    75→    75→
    76→    76→Canvas files (`.canvas`) use an open JSON format ([JSON Canvas spec](https://github.com/obsidianmd/jsoncanvas)) with 4 node types: **file** (vault references), **text** (markdown), **link** (URLs), and **group** (containers). Edges connect nodes with directional arrows. Since canvas files are plain JSON, they can be programmatically generated, manipulated, and queried.
    77→    77→
    78→    78→_Node Types: file, text, link, group — each with x/y/width/height positioning_
    79→    79→_Edge System: fromNode/toNode with side anchoring (top/right/bottom/left) and labels_
    80→    80→_Color System: 6 palette presets or hex values_
    81→    81→_Programmatic Tools: canvas_lib.py, obsidian-node-canvas, Advanced Canvas plugin_
    82→    82→_Source: [Canvas Help](https://help.obsidian.md/plugins/canvas), [Canvas API DeepWiki](https://deepwiki.com/obsidianmd/obsidian-api/4.1-canvas-api), [JSON Canvas GitHub](https://github.com/obsidianmd/jsoncanvas)_
    83→    83→
    84→    84→### Dataview Plugin (Query Engine)
    85→    85→
    86→    86→Dataview treats an Obsidian vault as a queryable database. It indexes YAML frontmatter and inline fields (`[key:: value]`) and provides both a DQL query language and a JavaScript API (DataviewJS). It now uses IndexedDB caching for near-instant startup on repeat visits.
    87→    87→
    88→    88→_Query Modes: DQL (table/list/task/calendar) and DataviewJS (full JavaScript)_
    89→    89→_Data Sources: YAML frontmatter, inline fields `[key:: value]`, tags, tasks_
    90→    90→_Caching: IndexedDB for fast startup on large vaults_
    91→    91→_Limitation: Read-only by design — cannot modify notes, only display/query_
    92→    92→_Source: [Dataview GitHub](https://github.com/blacksmithgu/obsidian-dataview), [Dataview Docs](https://blacksmithgu.github.io/obsidian-dataview/), [Dataview API](https://deepwiki.com/blacksmithgu/obsidian-dataview/4-api-reference)_
    93→    93→
    94→    94→### Templater Plugin (Template Automation)
    95→    95→
    96→    96→Templater (3.8M+ downloads, 4,616 GitHub stars) provides dynamic template insertion with JavaScript execution. It supports conditional logic, file manipulation, system commands, and user prompt inputs. Combined with Dataview, it transforms Obsidian into an automation platform.
    97→    97→
    98→    98→_Template Syntax: `<% %>` (variable expansion), `<%* %>` (JavaScript execution)_
    99→    99→_Capabilities: File creation, folder manipulation, date math, system commands, user prompts_
   100→   100→_Automation: Auto-apply templates on note creation, folder-based template matching_
   101→   101→_Source: [Templater GitHub](https://github.com/SilentVoid13/Templater), [Templater Scripts](https://github.com/mihaiconstantin/obsidian-templater-scripts)_
   102→   102→
